title: The difference between remove and discard
description:
What is the difference between remove and discard?

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `apply_removal(s, item, method)`, where `method` is the string `'remove'` or `'discard'`. Apply the named removal method for `item` to a copy of set `s`. If the call raises `KeyError`, return the string `'KeyError'`; otherwise return a SORTED list of the set's remaining elements. This demonstrates the real behavioral difference: `.remove()` raises `KeyError` when the item is missing, while `.discard()` silently does nothing.
hints: Both .remove() and .discard() take an item out of a set when it's present, but they disagree about what to do when the item is missing.
Wrap the removal call so you can catch what happens when the item isn't in the set, rather than letting your function crash.
Use a try/except KeyError around calling s.remove(item) or s.discard(item) based on the method argument, returning 'KeyError' if it's caught.
expected_behavior: Applies .remove() or .discard() (chosen by the method argument) to a copy of the set for the given item. Returns the string 'KeyError' if a KeyError was raised, otherwise a sorted list of what's left in the set.

hidden_tests.label: discard on a missing item does nothing
remove on a missing item raises KeyError
remove on a present item works normally

explanation: set.remove(item) raises KeyError if item is not in the set, while set.discard(item) removes it if present and otherwise does nothing at all - that silent-vs-noisy behavior on a missing element is the core difference between the two methods.
